steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added to the file.
successCriteria: The code must include a valid import statement that imports both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check that your import statement uses the correct syntax with curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main Accordion component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Accordion that returns null for now. Use TypeScript syntax and define it after the imports.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Make sure it returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Accordion component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named Accordion is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: Uses TypeScript syntax (explicit or inferred return type)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Accordion component. Returning null is a good starting point—we'll add the actual UI in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but something's missing. Make sure you've created a component named Accordion that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a functional component named Accordion that returns null.

steps.title: Define the AccordionItem interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'AccordionItem' with two properties: 'title' of type string and 'content' of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a type-safe interface that describes the structure of an accordion item.
successCriteria: The interface should be named 'AccordionItem' and include both 'title' and 'content' properties with correct string types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the AccordionItem interface with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface has both 'title' and 'content' properties, both typed as strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create an interface named 'AccordionItem' with 'title: string' and 'content: string' properties.

steps.title: Create sample accordion data
steps.instruction: Create a constant array named 'accordionData' with 2-3 AccordionItem objects. Place this array after the interface definition and before the component.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword to declare the array. Each object should have 'title' and 'content' properties that match the AccordionItem interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a typed array containing 2-3 accordion items that can be used for rendering in the component.
successCriteria: Array type is AccordionItem[] (explicit or inferred)
Each object has 'title' and 'content' string properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed data array that matches the AccordionItem interface. This will serve as the data source for your accordion component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the array 'accordionData'? Does it contain 2-3 objects? Does each object have both 'title' and 'content' string properties?
steps.feedbackWrong: The array wasn't created correctly. Remember to create a constant array named 'accordionData' with 2-3 objects that match the AccordionItem interface (each with 'title' and 'content' string properties).

steps.title: Initialize activeIndex state
steps.instruction: Inside the Accordion component, initialize a state variable named activeIndex using useState. Set its default value to null.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to specify the type for the state as number | null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Accordion component now has an activeIndex state variable initialized to null, ready to track which accordion item is open.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call inside the Accordion component that declares a state variable named activeIndex with a default value of null and proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the activeIndex state. This will allow us to track which accordion item is currently open.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check a few things: Did you name the state variable 'activeIndex'? Did you set the default value to null? Did you include the proper TypeScript type annotation?
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization doesn't match what we need. Remember to use useState with the name 'activeIndex', default value null, and proper TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Define the toggleAccordion handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Accordion component, define a function named toggleAccordion that takes an index parameter of type number and toggles the activeIndex state.
steps.hint: The function should check if the clicked index is already active, then set activeIndex to null to close it; otherwise set activeIndex to the clicked index.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleAccordion function is defined and ready to be used for handling accordion item clicks.
successCriteria: The toggleAccordion function should be defined inside the component, accept a number parameter, and update the activeIndex state appropriately.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the toggleAccordion handler function. This function will control which accordion item is open when users click on it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are a few issues. Make sure your toggleAccordion function accepts an index parameter of type number and properly toggles the activeIndex state by comparing the current activeIndex with the clicked index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleAccordion handler isn't defined correctly. You need to create a function that takes an index parameter and updates the activeIndex state based on whether that index is already active.

steps.title: Return the main wrapper div
steps.instruction: Inside your Accordion component, return a div element from the component's render function.
steps.hint: The component should return JSX. Add a return statement with a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Accordion component now returns a div element, providing the basic structure for the accordion.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element
The return statement is properly placed inside the component body
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the main wrapper div to your Accordion component. This provides the basic structure that will contain all the accordion items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element from the Accordion component. Check that your return statement is properly placed inside the component body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Accordion component needs to return JSX. Add a return statement with a div element to create the basic structure for your accordion.

steps.title: Map over accordionData to render items
steps.instruction: Inside the wrapper div, map over accordionData to render each item. Use the map method to iterate through the data array and return JSX for each item.
steps.hint: Use the map method on accordionData. For each item, you can return a div or other container element. The map callback should take each item and its index as parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The wrapper div now contains a map expression that iterates over accordionData and returns JSX for each item.
successCriteria: The code should include a map method called on accordionData inside the wrapper div, returning JSX for each item with a unique key prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used map to iterate over accordionData and render each item. This is the foundation for dynamically displaying accordion sections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the map method on accordionData inside the wrapper div and returning JSX for each item. Don't forget to include a key prop for each rendered item.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on this step only: inside the wrapper div, use the map method on accordionData to render each item. The map callback should return JSX for each accordion item.

steps.title: Create the accordion header button
steps.instruction: Inside the map function, create a button element for each accordion item. The button should display the item's title and call the toggleAccordion handler with the current index when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the map callback's index parameter as the argument to toggleAccordion. The button's text content should be the item's title property.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each accordion item will have a button that displays its title and can be clicked to trigger the toggle functionality.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created interactive header buttons for each accordion item. The buttons display the section titles and are wired to call the toggle handler with the correct index.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you create a button element? Does it display the item's title? Does the onClick handler call toggleAccordion with the current index?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on this step: Inside the map function, create a button element that shows the item's title and calls toggleAccordion(index) when clicked.

steps.title: Add conditional content display
steps.instruction: Inside the map callback, after the button, add a div that conditionally displays the item's content only when that item's index equals activeIndex.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator or logical AND (&&) to conditionally render the content div. The content should be inside the div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The content for each accordion item will only appear when its index matches the activeIndex state, creating the expand/collapse behavior.
successCriteria: Content div is rendered only when index matches activeIndex
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the accordion content. The content now only appears when its section is active.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your conditional logic. Make sure the content div only renders when the item's index equals activeIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional content display wasn't implemented correctly. Review how to conditionally render elements based on state in React.

steps.title: Add basic styling classes
steps.instruction: Add className attributes to the wrapper div, button, and content div for basic styling. Use 'accordion' for the wrapper, 'accordion-button' for the button, and 'accordion-content' for the content div.
steps.hint: Add className attributes to the existing JSX elements. Remember to add the content div inside the map function after the button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding className attributes
Content here
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion will have CSS class names applied to its wrapper, buttons, and content divs, ready for styling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the basic styling classes. The accordion now has proper class names for CSS styling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some class names, but not all required ones. Make sure the wrapper div, button, and content div all have their respective className attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required className attributes are missing. Add className="accordion" to the wrapper div, className="accordion-button" to the button, and className="accordion-content" to the content div.

steps.title: Export the Accordion component
steps.instruction: Export the Accordion component as the default export from this file.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax to make the Accordion component available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Accordion component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The code includes 'export default Accordion;' at the end of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the Accordion component as the default export. This makes it available for import in other files using 'import Accordion from "./Accordion";'.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're exporting the Accordion component as the default export using 'export default Accordion;'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Accordion component needs to be exported as the default export. Add 'export default Accordion;' at the end of the file.
